messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — root cause was the ETL partition shuffle that dropped span metadata and a subsequent aggregation job that silently reduced counts. I want to lock owners, timelines, and detection so this doesn't recur. Proposed actionable items below; reply with confirmations or updates.

alex: ACTIONS (proposed)
- ETL routing fix (ensure partition keys preserved + add integration test): owner = maya, target = 3 business days
- Aggregation correctness guardrails (query-level sanity checks + alert): owner = jon, target = 5 business days
- Observability alerts & runbook (detect missing spans + auto-escalation): owner = nora, target = 2 business days
- Backfill plan & cost estimate (if needed): owner = sam, target = 1 week
- Add recurring job to surface span-loss trends (weekly): owner = nora/jon, target = 2 weeks

maya: I can take ETL routing. I already started a branch that preserves the original partition_key during shuffle. Will push a draft today. Need help with a unit test harness for shuffled partitions.

jon: I’ll own aggregation checks. Suggest we add a nightly sanity query that fails if total_spans deviates >1% from expected baseline for a namespace. Quick SQL I used in the past:
```sql
SELECT namespace, sum(span_count) as total_spans
FROM aggregated_spans
WHERE event_date >= current_date - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY namespace
HAVING abs(sum(span_count) - expected_weekly_spans) > expected_weekly_spans * 0.01;
```
I can turn that into an alert in the observability infra — will prototype today.

nora: For alerts/runbook: we should create two tiers — (1) span-loss growth alert (emails + slack p95) and (2) data-correctness regression (pager). Also add instructions to validate the ETL partition keys and aggregation totals. I'll sketch the runbook and attach to the postmortem doc.

sam: For the backfill: before we commit, can we quantify how many partitions are affected? If it's small we can do a targeted backfill; if large we might choose to approximate or skip depending on customer impact. I can run a partition check job once the ETL fix is in a staging run. ETA for my estimate: 48 hours after ETL fix landed.

alex: Nice. A few clarifications:
- maya, please include a small integration test that runs the shuffle on 10k synthetic spans and asserts partition_key is identical pre/post.
- jon, make the alert run hourly for the first week after deploy and then scale back to nightly if stable.
- nora, include escalation matrix (on-call -> eng-sre -> analytics lead).
- sam, add cost estimate for the backfill options in your doc.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: staging deploy queued by maya-branch/etl-shuffle-fix at 2026-03-23T15:40:12Z

maya: pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/412 — tests failing on edge case, working through it. Will ping when green.

jon: prototype alert query pushed as a prometheus recording rule and a grafana alert panel in a PR: https://github.com/redwood/observability/pull/98

nora: runbook draft uploaded to the postmortem doc (link): https://redwood.internal/docs/postmortems/pm-2026-03-22-span-loss — included escalation steps + checklist.

sam: ran partition scanner on current prod snapshot in staging after pruning — estimate: ~1200 partitions touched, likely doable as targeted backfill. Cost estimate ~ $1.2k compute + ~2 hours ops. Will draft runbook steps for the backfill.

alex: OK — owners confirmed. I'll convert these items into the remediation tracker and assign tickets:
- RDW-2345: ETL preserve partition keys (owner: maya) due 2026-03-26
- RDW-2346: Aggregation sanity alerts (owner: jon) due 2026-03-28
- RDW-2347: Observability runbook + alerts (owner: nora) due 2026-03-25
- RDW-2348: Backfill plan + estimate (owner: sam) due 2026-04-01

alex: Let's have a short 15min sync in 48h to check PRs and alert proofs. If anything blocks, update the tracker or ping here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maya: will update PR and ping when tests pass.

jon: will wire the alert to channel #observability and add the hourly/temp logic.

nora: I'll add runbook link to RDW-2347 and set up the pager rotation.

sam: will prepare the backfill playbook and cost breakdown.

alex: closing the thread — will post ticket links once created. Keep posting status updates here so we have a single place to follow remediation progress.
